title: Isospectral majorization and isoperimetric inequalities for coherent states on the Bloch sphere
abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}_{N}$ be the $(N+1)$-dimensional Hilbert space of analytic polynomials of degree at most $N$. This is the natural environment to define $SU(2)$ (Bloch) coherent states. Let $Q_{ρ}$ be the Husimi function of a density operator $ρ$ on $% \mathcal{P}_{N}$. We prove an isospectral version of Lieb-Solovej inequality: if $ρ^{\downarrow }$ is obtained by placing the eigenvalues of $ρ$ in decreasing order along the monomial basis, then \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb{C}}Φ(Q_{ρ}(z))\,dm(z)\leq \int_{\mathbb{C}}Φ(Q_{ρ^{\downarrow }}(z))\,dm(z) \end{equation*}% for every convex function $Φ$ on $[0,1]$. Applying the corresponding reversed inequality to the concave function $Φ(t)=-t\log t$ gives the Wehrl entropy. In the process it is show that the output state of $ρ$ under Lieb-Solovej's channel is majorized by the output of the state $ρ^{\downarrow }$.   As an application, among all measurable subsets of the sphere having a fixed area, spherical caps maximize every partial sum of the eigenvalues of Toeplitz operators with symbol $1_Ω$. Equivalently, caps maximize all Ky Fan norms, leading to the sharp inequalities, previously known for $r=1$: \begin{equation*} \sum_{j=1}^{r}λ_{j}(Ω) \leq r-\sum_{k=0}^{r-1}(r-k)\binom{N+1}{k} m(Ω)^{k}\bigl(1-m(Ω)\bigr)^{N+1-k}. \end{equation*} This implies isoperimetric inequalities for all Schatten sums of $T_Ω$, obtained without using the spherical isoperimetric inequality.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a fixed-spectrum majorization theory for coherent states on the Bloch sphere. By proving an isospectral version of the Lieb-Solovej inequality, it shows that passive rearrangement minimizes entropy. This spectral result is then applied to derive sharp isoperimetric inequalities for Toeplitz operators associated with measurable subsets of the sphere.
main_problem: The paper establishes isospectral majorization relationships and derives sharp isoperimetric inequalities for coherent states defined on the Bloch sphere.
main_result: It proves a fixed-spectrum Lieb-Solovej inequality, showing that passive rearrangement minimizes certain entropy measures, which in turn yields isoperimetric bounds for Toeplitz operators related to spherical caps.
method: The analysis uses functional inequalities (convex/concave functions $\Phi$) applied to the Husimi function and leverages majorization theory ($\prec$) derived from spectral properties of Toeplitz operators.
model_or_system: The system is based on density operators $ho$ acting on the Hilbert space of analytic polynomials $P_N$, which models coherent states on the Bloch sphere ($	ext{SU}(2)$). The analysis involves Toeplitz operators $T_\Omega$ defined by subsets $\Omega$ of the sphere.
key_observables: Husimi function ($Q_ho(z)$), Wehrl entropy ($S_W(ho)$), and partial sums of eigenvalues ($\sum \lambda_j(\Omega)$) of Toeplitz operators.
important_parameters: The polynomial degree $N$, the rank of the density operator $	ext{Rank}(ho)=r$, and the measure/area $m(\Omega)$ of the subset $\Omega$.
main_assumptions: The results are derived for fixed spectra, extending previous rank-1 results. The extension to general convex functions relies on approximating them with piecewise linear functions.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the Lieb-Solovej inequality (comparing $ho$ to its passive rearrangement $ho_{\downarrow}$) to establish entropy minimization, culminating in the application of this spectral theory to derive sharp isoperimetric inequalities for Toeplitz operators on the sphere.
why_interesting: This work connects fundamental concepts from quantum information geometry (coherent states, entropy) with classical geometric inequalities (isoperimetry), providing powerful tools applicable to characterizing optimal state preparations or spatial distributions in quantum systems.
